title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section IV (manuscript p. 568) restarts in abstract form what the previous page did concretely for SL(2,Z)^. It recasts it as a setting for an arbitrary profinite group.

Setting. Let G be a profinite group topologically generated by rho and sigma, with rho^6 = sigma^4 = 1 and rho^3 = sigma^2 =: -1. Equivalently, G is a quotient of SL(2,Z)^, the profinite completion of the amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. One may think of rho = ST of order 6 and sigma = S of order 4. The special case rho^3 = sigma^2 = 1 means G is a quotient of PSL(2,Z)^ = (Z/3 * Z/2)^, the (oriented) cartographic group of trivalent maps / dessins.

The involution tau. tau is an automorphism of G with tau(sigma) = sigma^{-1} = -sigma and tau(rho) = sigma rho^{-1} sigma^{-1}, written ^sigma(rho^{-1}). In SL(2,Z) this is conjugation by J = diag(1,-1), an element of determinant -1 in GL(2,Z). I checked it on matrices: S^{-1} = J S J, and J(ST)J = S (ST)^{-1} S^{-1} = [[0,1],[-1,1]]. Asking that tau exist on G amounts to asking that G be a tau-stable quotient of SL(2,Z)^.

Consequences of the defining relations:
- tau^2 = 1. Indeed tau^2(rho) = sigma^{-1}(sigma rho sigma^{-1}) sigma = rho.
- tau(eps0) = eps0^{-1} and tau(eps1) = eps1^{-1}.

Here eps0 = sigma rho = -sigma^{-1} rho, which is -T, i.e. -1 times the cusp (parabolic) generator. Also eps1 = rho sigma, which equals each of the conjugates ^sigma(eps0), ^{sigma^{-1}}(eps0) and ^rho(eps0).

The extension. G' = {1,tau} . G (semidirect product), giving 1 -> G -> G' -> {1,tau} -> 1. This is the analogue of GL(2,Z)^ over SL(2,Z)^. Geometrically, G' encodes the real structure / complex conjugation on the orbifold M_{1,1}.

Margin remark. It is preferable to use tau' = int(sigma^{-1}) o tau, i.e. conjugation by [[0,1],[1,0]]. This gives tau'(rho) = rho^{-1}, tau'(sigma) = sigma^{-1}, tau'(eps0) = eps1^{-1} and tau'(eps1) = eps0^{-1}, all of which I verified.

The group B. Define B_{rho,sigma} inside Aut(G) x Z^* as the set of pairs (u, mu) such that:
- u(eps0) = eps0^mu exactly;
- u(sigma) is conjugate in G to sigma^mu;
- u(rho) is conjugate in G to rho^mu.

This is a subgroup. It is exactly the shape of the Galois action on pi_1^orb(M_{1,1} over Qbar) = SL(2,Z)^:
- the cusp inertia eps0 is sent to its chi(g)-th power (with a normalized choice of tangential base point);
- the inertias at j = 1728 (sigma) and j = 0 (rho) are sent to conjugates of their mu-th powers.

So B_{rho,sigma} is a genus-(1,1), modular-group analogue of GT, attached to each (finite) quotient G. Next page: since rho^6 = 1, rho^mu = rho^{eps3(mu)}, and similarly sigma^mu = eps2(mu) sigma. Hence the third condition becomes conjugacy to rho^{±1}, which can be realised by elements alpha or tau.alpha of G'. A Proposition characterising B by elements alpha, beta follows. The purpose is the 'variations on the loop equation': finite or quotient-level analogues of the GT conditions for the modular tower.
errors: No mathematical errors found. All stated identities check in SL(2,Z), using the convention that sigma(x) means conjugation by sigma.

The step 'which implies tau^2 = 1' is valid because G is topologically generated by rho and sigma. The existence of tau on an arbitrary quotient G is an extra hypothesis (tau-stability of the kernel), not automatic.

Minor notational looseness: the same letter tau is used for the automorphism of SL(2,Z)^ and the induced one on G. The third condition in (7) is written with G (possibly G') ambiguously; the next page clarifies that conjugacy to rho^{-1} is realised via G'.

ideas.what: Presentation of SL(2,Z)^ (resp. PSL(2,Z)^) by rho, sigma with rho^6 = sigma^4 = 1 and rho^3 = sigma^2; quotients viewed as 'modular' or cartographic groups
ideas.modern_name: Profinite completion of the amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6; cartographic group for the trivalent case
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Serre, Trees); cartographic group: Grothendieck, Esquisse; Malgoire–Voisin
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups, SL(2,Z) as cartographic group of the 'triangulated' case)

ideas.what: Determinant -1 involution tau acting by sigma -> sigma^{-1}, rho -> ^sigma(rho^{-1}), and the extension G' = {1,tau}.G mimicking GL(2,Z)^ / complex conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Real structure on M_{1,1}; GL(2,Z)^ as extension of SL(2,Z)^ by Z/2; 'oriented vs non-oriented' cartographic groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Grothendieck (Esquisse) for non-oriented cartographic groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions oriented / non-oriented cartographic groups; this specific formula is unsure

ideas.what: Group B_{rho,sigma} of pairs (u, mu) normalising cusp inertia exactly and elliptic inertias up to conjugacy, defined for every quotient G of SL(2,Z)^
ideas.modern_name: Genus-one / modular analogue of GT (Teichmüller–Galois action on pi_1(M_{1,1})); level-wise 'GT-shadow'-type groups attached to finite quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Galois action on pi_1(M_{1,1}): Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (Gamma-hat T), Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps; finite-quotient GT-shadows: Dolgushev and coauthors (2020s)
ideas.where_published: Idea of the Teichmüller tower at level (1,1) is in the Esquisse; this explicit group is in the unpublished Longue Marche sequel

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines, for an arbitrary (finite) quotient G of SL(2,Z)^ (or PSL(2,Z)^ = cartographic group), a group B_{rho,sigma} of 'admissible' pairs (automorphism, cyclotomic-type unit). These are the conditions a Galois/GT-type action must satisfy at that finite level. This is a quotient-wise or 'shadow' approach to GT-type groups for the modular group / M_{1,1}. It anticipates the recent GT-shadow program, which treats finite quotients of B_4/PB_4 or F_2, but in the genus-one/modular setting.
missed.quote: B_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(𝔊) × Ẑ* = {(u,μ) | u(ε0)=ε0^μ, u(σ) conjugué dans 𝔊 à σ^μ, u(ρ) conjugué dans 𝔊 à ρ^μ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Finite-level GT-shadow computations are an active topic (Dolgushev et al.). A modular-group (SL(2,Z)^) version tied to Galois orbits of modular or trivalent dessins is less developed. Grothendieck's framework, including the tau-extension for the real structure, could supply that version.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up a clean, correct, quotient-wise GT-type group for SL(2,Z)^ quotients, including the real involution. It is conceptually in line with known ideas (Galois action on pi_1(M_{1,1}), Gamma-hat T) but is an unpublished explicit formulation. The calculations themselves are routine.
transcription_corrections: In (2), the second relation should be read as tau(rho) = ^sigma(rho^{-1}) = sigma rho^{-1} sigma^{-1} (conjugation), not sigma applied to rho^{-1} as a product.
The parenthesis after (2) most likely says that tau of G is 'passed to the quotient' from the automorphism tau of SL(2,Z)^, not 'tau of G'.
Equation number (6) appears twice: the first for G' = {1,tau}.G, the second for the exact sequence (probably (6) and (6')).
The first margin note reads roughly 'Ceci signifie que G est un quotient de SL(2,Z)^'.

The second margin note's tau' should be tau' = sigma^{-1} tau (inner by sigma^{-1} composed with tau). With that reading, tau'(rho) = rho^{-1}, tau'(sigma) = sigma^{-1}, tau'(eps0) = eps1^{-1} and tau'(eps1) = eps0^{-1}, which I verified.
In (7), the third condition's conjugating group is written ambiguously, possibly G' (with a mark). The next page indicates conjugation by elements of G' (alpha or tau.alpha) when eps3(mu) = -1.
